question: What is the percentage of 's' character in the carbon atom of acetylene?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Acetylene, also known as ethyne, has the chemical formula C₂H₂.
 
• Each carbon atom in acetylene forms two sigma (σ) bonds and two pi (π) bonds.
 
• In acetylene, the bonding involves sp hybridization for carbon atoms.
 
• Sp hybridization implies that each carbon atom has 50% s-character and 50% p-character in its hybrid orbitals.
 
• Therefore, the percentage of s-character in the carbon atom of acetylene is 50%, which corresponds to the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acetylene**: A colorless gas used as a fuel and a chemical building block.
 
• **Hybridization**: The concept of mixing atomic orbitals to form new hybrid orbitals suitable for the pairing of electrons to form chemical bonds.
 
• **Sigma Bond (σ bond)**: A single covalent bond formed by the direct overlap of atomic orbitals, resulting in a region of electron density along the axis connecting the two bonded nuclei.
 
• **Pi Bond (π bond)**: A type of covalent bond that results from the sideways overlap of p orbitals, which creates regions of electron density above and below the axis of the bonded atoms.
 
• **Sp Hybridization**: A type of orbital hybridization where one s orbital and one p orbital mix to form two equivalent sp hybrid orbitals, each having 50% s-character and 50% p-character.
